cv:
Diego Herrera · ML engineer · Guadalajara, Mexico
Insurance company (2021 – present, 5 years): claims document classification with LLMs, model evaluation, on-prem deployments.
reply:
Hi Sofia,

1) I built a claims-intake classifier that reads incoming claim documents and routes them to the right adjuster team. It handles about 1,200 documents a day, and I owned the model choice, the prompts and the evaluation.
2) We have 400 claims labeled by senior adjusters. Every model or prompt change runs against them; macro F1 went from 0.78 to 0.89.
3) The insurer required that documents never leave their network, so I had to make it work on-prem.
4) For that I compared Llama 3.1 70B and Qwen 2.5 72B running on our own GPUs against a hosted model on the same 400 claims: Qwen was 3 points below the hosted model at about a quarter of the cost, so we shipped Qwen. Policy numbers and dates are parsed with regular expressions, not by the model.
5) Guadalajara, Mexico. $38/hour. English 9/10. 6 hours of overlap.

Best,
Diego

expected.why: Meets every criterion including the nice-to-have: he ran and compared open-weight language models on his own labeled set and reports the result.
